Operation Racketeer

By: Joy Summers | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Rogue cops, an antipoaching unit, extrajudicial killings to claim bonuses and danger pay. The story of two building contractors and a good cop, whose lives were destroyed when they were set up as rhin

Unique Selling Point:
The case studies will go on camera, we have unseen footage, and all the court documents vindicating the men who claimed innocence for over 9 years but were smeared by an NGO with ulterior motives.

Summary:
Overview
Around 2014, police officer Christopher Gumbi was seconded to take part in a rural safety operation in the Jozini cluster. He had already been involved in the process of gathering information about an operation involving the rendition of foreign nationals from Mozambique being lured into game parks in KZN and then killing them under the guise of those persons being suspected of being involved in rhino horn poaching. The purpose of the persons involved in the rendition and the murder of foreign nationals was to recover rewards paid to informers and recover danger allowances.

But Gumbi was a problem to a group of police and private security who had a lot to hide and a lot to lose, because they were doing just that- cashing in on money from an NGO and danger pay from the police, by falsely accusing innocent victims of rhino poaching.

Their victims -and the stories of Wiseman Mageba and Dumisani Gwala if exposed would pose a threat to the rogue police and their security buddies who claim to be hero’s saving the rhino, when all they were really doing was lining their own pockets.

Our story weaves Gumbi’s story with that of Gwala and Mageba. All three have been vindicated by the courts and we have all the documents. Gumbi has already been paid damages, but he left the police.
In July 2023 Gwala and Mageba were vindicated by the courts and now they have in Feb 2024 served summons against SAPS and the NPA for a large damages claim.


Further information:
WISEMAN MAGEBA AND DUMISANI GWALA.
Gwala was set up by Warrant officer JP Roux and an agent who later mysteriously died. The rhino horn from KZN Ezemvelo Parks that was used to set him up disappeared. When he was arrested he was shot eleven times in front of his pregnant wife and his seven year old daughter. Gwala should have died, but he didn’t. His wife later lost her child from the stress of everything. ( there is footage from the shooting that has never been seen – it comes from the police bodycam and we have access to this footage)

His case was manipulated and moved from one court to another and when it became clear in 2016 that the court case would reveal the shocking truth that Gwala and Mageba were falsely arrested so that the rogue cops could cash in on the danger pay and the bonusses for arresting rhino poachers, they paid an NGO to smear the men.
It was a full on apartheid style disinformation campaign, says Megan Carr, who at first thought Warrant officer JP ROUX and Jamie Joseph from the NGO Save the wild, were hero’s. But as she dug deeper using her own funds, she realized that in fact the real picture was quite different and Joseph was paid to muddy the water. Mostly the media lapped it up, and that is when Carr decided to go all in, and fund a good criminal lawyer to unearth the police footage and give her a true picture of events so she didn’t think she was going quite mad. Carte Blanche investigates this story that highlights the shadowy world of rogue cops, rhino horns, an apartheid style disinformation campaign and the difficulty that poor people falsely accused have when they come up against this shadow state.


Extra Budget Items:
Complex logistics as the story takes place in far Northern KZN and lots of travel time cuts into the shoot. Still have to get right of replies in Gauteng as well from the NPA and SAPS

OPERATION RACKETEER FINAL SCRIPT FOR BROADCAST:
Operation Racketeer FINAL SCRIPT 23rd May 2024

Voice over One
Game reserves in KZN- at the mercy of rhino poachers.

A private fund paid out bonuses for the successful arrests of alleged suspects

Evidence, including case numbers, shows more than a million Rand paid in just one year

Alice Wild
There were bonuses being paid for the successful arrests of rhino poachers. It was a fund that was set up with good intentions by really good people and this fund was manipulated

Voice over Two
The high profile arrest of KwaZulu Natal’s alleged rhino poaching kingpin is trumpeted by an anti poaching unit, and the police are seen as heroes.

Clare link
But were these the hero’s we thought they were, or is there a different, more inconvenient far darker narrative?

Wiseman Mageba
The world knows us, we are the kingpins, but at the end the truth was coming

Voice over Three
Deaths under suspicious circumstances… a crime intelligence officer suspects his own colleagues.

Gumbi
That was their mission, to make sure no one comes after them in their dealings.

Voice over Four
He launches an investigation but is set up and arrested before he can finish

Gumbi
It ended up looking like I was involved in this,
but it was actually them.

Voice over five
A conservation researcher, and key witness questions the narrative.

Alice Wild
Anyone who has tried to shine any light on this story, has either been assassinated or intimidated, their reputations destroyed.

Voice over six
And questions raised on the role of a wildlife NGO and its high profile founder.

Claire
If it turned out to be true then how were they all acquitted?
Jamie
This is South Africa! How are they all acquitted? How are they always all acquitted?

Alice Wild
South Africans wanted a perpetrator, they loved her story. She published a photograph of a naked man, bleeding from being shot and the SA audience loved it

FADE TO BLACK OVER PHOTOGRAPH.

Voice over seven
In 2014, former crime intelligence officer, Christopher Gumbi, was deployed in Jozini, to help combat organised crime along the border with Mozambique.

Christopher Gumbi
While we were working, crimes were being committed right under our noses.

These crimes were organised by professionals.

We were there working as Crime Intelligence, look at it like this my sister, Crime Intelligence versus Organised (Crime.) These are both heavyweights.

Voice over eight
It appeared to him that Mozambicans were being framed by members of organised crime.

Gumbi
They took people across the border. They would bring them into the reserve, foreigners from Mozambique. They were then found murdered inside the reserves and accused of rhino poaching.

Voice over nine
What Gumbi saw at the scenes didn't make sense.

Gumbi
Then you find that person lying dead. The rhino horn is missing. Who took the rhino horn? How? This kept happening.
That is when my focus shifted.
Claire
So you have identified it was organised crime, was that a shock to you?
Gumbi
Yes that is how it was. I was confused. Our colleagues are doing this. Our white colleagues. Were they using their skin colour to pull this off? And I decided that something needs to be done, no one is above the law.

Voice over ten
But soon afterwards he was arrested using what’s known as an entrapment warrant. Issued by the National Prosecuting Authority, they’re used to detect, investigate or prevent an offence.

Gumbi was arrested by this man- JP Van Zyl Roux and charged with the unlawful possession of rhino horns, fraud and robbery.

In an instant, Gumbi’s life and reputation were destroyed.

Clair
What would you like to see happen?
Gumbi
I want the truth to be revealed.

Voice over 11
A court and an internal disciplinary hearing later found Gumbi not guilty. But he waited years before the high court ruled he'd been an honest witness and awarded him damages.

Link
The judgement in favour of Mr Gumbi says that the SAPS member that issued the warrant of entrapment behaved dishonestly, unlawfully, maliciously pursuing a fruitless prosecution, but what is clear is that this was a pattern and the victims were usually poor and black

Voice over 12
When Wiseman Mageba sat down with us he was nervous. He hasn't told his story before.


Wiseman Mageba
I am very afraid.. I never know when they will come for me....
They can come at any time to shoot me as happened to other

Voice over thirteen
In 2014, Mageba was arrested in 2014.. At the time he owned a construction business and crucially to our investigation, an electrician he used called Dumisani Gwala, was arrested on the same day.

Up sound

Mageba was arrested while fixing his car at the side of the road. Officially he was suspected of carrying rhino horn but in this police video of his arrest, there’s no sign of it. Mageba claims that, at one point the police put a bag in his car.

Up sound

After asking what they were doing, these heavily armed men arrived and took him into custody.

Up sound of the arrest.

Van Zyl Roux- the officer who’s arrested crime intelligence officer, Christopher Gumbi - was central to this arrest too. He says Mageba and the electrician, Dumisani Gwala, bought rhino horn from police agents.

But our investigation revealed that this man, one of the agents, is a former crime intelligence officer, fired for extortion in 2021.

Voice over 14
Mageba spent 838 days in a police cell.

Mageba
Two years, three months is a long time. On the 28th of July 2023, it's where we finalised the case, it's where the judgement came to us.

Voice over 15
In 2023 he was found not guilty. All ten charges ruled to be inadmissible.

Mageba
I lost my everything. I lost my company, my family, my wife and kids, so that was a very bad time for me.

Voice over 16
The court questioned what had happened to the 6 rhino horns used by the police, why there had been no paper trail, or attempt to infiltrate the alleged syndicate he was supposed to be a part of.

Mageba
Then I said oh thank God. Actually we are the victims.
They need to get the victims to cover themselves

Voice over 17
Dumisani Gwala was shot at 11 times during his arrest. Six bullets hit their mark

Gwala
The way things panned out, their intention was to kill me.

Voice over 17
He was, according to the police, the rhino poaching kingpin.

Claire
As we sit here today, you didn’t want to talk to us, why not?
Dumisani Gwala
I have suffered a lot, with my family, a lot. Even now I am not sleeping at home. I sleep in the forest. What has happened is that we were paraded in the media, the whole world knows my face.

Voice over 18
And the reason his face is so well known, is down to a wildlife activist called Jamie Joseph.

A South African who is the founder of Saving the Wild, an NGO registered in New Zealand, she built a campaign around Gwala, raising over a million US Dollars

Jamie Joseph
He is responsible for 80% of the horns that go through KZN province.

Dumisani Gwala
Jamie Joseph, she's an animal. I don't have the power to do anything to her. When I see her I have to run, because I never know what she is going to do.
Link
Convict Dumisani Gwala as a rhino poaching kingpin is her mantra, and a movie about her campaign is being planned. Except there is a problem, Jamie Joseph’s ending is not working out quite as she had hoped. Gwala has been acquitted, and now has a damages claim against the state

Alice Wild
She would follow Dumisane Gwala into the lavatories, Dumisani Gwala would say leave me alone and the next day they would print a picture in the Newspaper to say Dumisani Gwala threatens the journalist

Claire
What was the purpose of your campaign on social media when it came to Dumisani Gwala?
Jamie Joseph
People needed to understand that he had all these magistrates on his payroll and police officers and we thought that if we put it in the public domain and gave it a big enough spotlight, we hoped that he wouldn’t get away with it.

Claire
So do you have evidence that Dumisani Gwala had magistrates on their payroll. Do we know that for a fact

Jamie Joseph
Of course. It was all over the news, the person who was paying the bribes to the magistrate and the prosecutors and taking money from people like Gwala and police officer Gumbi was the defence attorney’s nephew,

Voice over 19
The evidence Joseph is referring to, came from a single whistleblower who claims to have handed money to magistrates on Gwala’s behalf.

Jamie Joseph
So the whistleblower came forward and he actually gave one exclusive interview to BBC and the sworn affidavit, after that he did a polygraph and the police investigated everything he said in his affidavit and it all turned out to be true.

Voice over 20
Except the whistleblower is a criminal and was in jail at the time he claimed to be handing cash to the magistrates. He later retracted his statement in an affidavit.

Alice Wild
It's very reminiscent of an apartheid style disinformation campaign, so everything that is ever said you can turn around 180% round.

Voice over 21
Joseph seems to have mastered the art of blending fact with fiction. Take for example the official police video of Gwala’s arrest, which I had not seen when I interviewed her.

Jamie Joseph
Have you seen the arrest video?
Claire
No I haven’t.
Jamie Joseph
He wasn’t viciously attacked. He was the one beating a police officer to death
Claire
To death?

Jamie Joseph
In the video you see the horns being thrown and beating this police officer almost to death.

Voice over 22
In affidavits, the police said they were going to Gwala’s house to collect the money from undercover deals they’d done with him, and to hand over another horn for the next deal.

But in the police video which we have slowed down, there is no evidence of money changing hands. What can be seen is the fired crime intelligence officer in a red shirt placing a bag into Gwala’s boot.

Gwala removes the bag and pushes it back at the officer, who then opens the drivers side of the car and leans in.

He is still holding the bag and Gwala appears confused.

GWALA
Right after that I saw a policeman come out of the back of their car and started shooting at me, that’s how I got arrested. That is how I lost everything.

Up sound video Get down wena

Voice over 23
The police grab Gwala and say get down dog, we are going to shoot you.

A scuffle ensues and a horn appears on the ground. We don't know how it gets there, and we don't see- as Jamie Joseph told me, Gwala almost beating a cop to death.

Carte Blanche has gone through the video frame by frame and it shows Gwala trying to get away, his wheels spinning in the sand as 3 weapons are pointed at him. He is unarmed and shot at eleven times.

Up sound
Shoot that guy man! Shoot that bastard. Shots fired.

Voice over 24
Eight years after his arrest, the courts found the evidence against Gwala inadmissible. Crucially it found that at no stage had either of the accused sold rhino horns. Gwala was found not guilty on all counts except a charge of resisting arrest.

Claire
To be honest your campaign went in hard. Would you apologise to him if you were told that you were wrong?
Jamie Joseph
I wasn’t wrong!

Voice over 25
Van Zyl Roux, the investigating officer, believes he wasn't wrong either. He says the evidence was not admitted because of a technicality.

In a written answer to us, he added that Gumbi’s claims of his involvement in organised crime are libellous and denied.

Mageba and Gwala still live in fear. There are unexplained deaths. In 2023, a businessman called Mackson Chirwa, who helped pay their legal costs was assassinated. His murder remains unsolved

Up sound Mackson Chirwa
Why are you taking the photos because you don't know me. No, I am not shouting.

Voice over 26
Jamie Joseph says she was accosted by him outside Court, but this video suggests that he was asking her to stop filming him. He filed an intimidation charge against her.

Jamie Joseph
Gwala, he lives by the gun, he will die by the gun. He will end up the same way his business partner, the hitman ended up. I am more worried about the sanctity of the courts.

Voice over 27
Joseph doesnt trust the judgements we have relied upon. She is determined to prove her claims of corrupt court officials and says the judgements are baseless.
She is astounded that we’re questioning her narrative.

Jamie Joseph
But the way you were talking about Gwala it's like he got to somebody, and his hitman and business partner have very high connections in politics?
Claire
So are you saying Carte Blanche is being influenced? What are you saying?
Jamie Joseph
I don't know who Gwala can get to, ok?
Claire
So he got to Carte Blanche in your mind?
Jamie Joseph
It sounds to me like you are trying to create a story to make Gwala look good

Voice over 28.
The investigating officer, JP Van Zyl Roux was fired from the police in 2017. He says the reason for his dismissal was unrelated to this case and he was unfairly dismissed.
He denied he received any bonuses from the police, and that the imputation of apartheid era police tactics are vexatious and scurrilous.

Meanwhile the movie inspired by Jamie Joseph, continues.

Claire
Let's talk about your movie that is in the pipeline?
Jamie Joseph
Why are we talking about my movie?
Claire
Because I want to wrap it up, you said you wanted to know if we are going to talk about
JJ
But now it sounds like there is a witch-hunt and I dont know yet because we will see what the final thing looks like, we will see if all my stuff is edited you know…


Claire
Do you want to talk to us or not Jamie?
Jamie Joseph
Because we wouldn't have lost all those rhino’s if we had people like JP Roux working in KZN and Gwala was locked up in jail, but keep going!
Claire
Actually I think I am done. I think I am actually done! Ya

Voice over 29
Gwala and Mageba are taking the Minister of Police, Minister of Justice and the NPA to court, claiming wrongful and unlawful arrest, entrapment, torture, and attempted murder.

Our questions to SAPS remain unanswered. The NPA says that due to the pending civil suit they will not be commenting.

KZN’s rhinos are still being killed. In 2023, 307 rhinos were lost in Hluhluwe iMfolozi Parks. There were 49 arrests made.

THE END 18 minutes


PROMO ONE

Voice over
Men accused of being KZN’s rhino poaching kingpins speak out for the first time after being acquitted

Alice Wild 22 00
People didn’t bother to ever check, the same story was repeated over and over but who would believe a black man, uneducated against a white Afrikaans policeman whose father was a brigadier

Up sound Jamie Joseph
Dumisani Gwala is a rhino poaching kingpin you have never heard of. He is responsible for 80% of the horns that go through KZN province.

Voice over
And a self styled corruption buster who ran a campaign against them is unapologetic

Claire
To be honest your campaign went in hard so I am saying would you apologise to him if you were told that you were wrong?
JAMIE JOSEPH
I wasn’t wrong!


PROMO TWO
A man accused of being an accomplice to a rhino poaching kingpin, lost everything when he was wrongly arrested. A decade later he speaks out

Mageba
Then I stayed there almost the rest of my life, two years, three months
Claire whispers
Two years and three months?
Mageba
Since 2014, until on the 28th of July 2023, it's where we finalised the case and the judgement came to us.

And a former warrant officer stumbles across crime scenes that point to his colleagues.

Gumbi
Then you find that person shot and the rhino horn is missing. They are lying dead, who took the rhino horn? How? This kept happening.
Claire
So you have identified it was organised crime, was that a shock to you?
Gumbi
Yes that is how it was. I was confused. Our colleagues are doing this. Our white colleagues. Were they using their skin colour to pull this off? And I decided that something needs to be done, no one is above the law.

PROMO THREE
Voice over
They were called the rhino poaching kingpins.
Wiseman Mageba
I am very afraid.. I never know when they will come for me....
They can come at any time to shoot me as happened to other

Voice over
It took a decade in the courts, and they lost everything. For the first time the men at the heart of this story, speak to Carte Blanche

Gwala
Their intention was to kill me.
Claire
To be honest your campaign went in hard so I am saying would you apologise to him if you were told that you were wrong?
JAMIE JOSEPH
I wasn’t wrong!

26 May 2024 TX Date: 0000-00-00 Script: OPERATION RACKETEER FINAL SCRIPT FOR BROADCAST: Operation Racketeer FINAL SCRIPT 23rd May 2024 Voice over One Game reserves in KZN- at the mercy of rhino poachers. A private fund paid out bonuses for the successful arrests of alleged suspects Evidence, including case numbers, shows more than a million Rand paid in just one year Alice Wild There were bonuses being paid for the successful arrests of rhino poachers. It was a fund that was set up with good intentions by really good people and this fund was manipulated Voice over Two The high profile arrest of KwaZulu Natal’s alleged rhino poaching kingpin is trumpeted by an anti poaching unit, and the police are seen as heroes. Clare link But were these the hero’s we thought they were, or is there a different, more inconvenient far darker narrative? Wiseman Mageba The world knows us, we are the kingpins, but at the end the truth was coming Voice over Three Deaths under suspicious circumstances… a crime intelligence officer suspects his own colleagues. Gumbi That was their mission, to make sure no one comes after them in their dealings. Voice over Four He launches an investigation but is set up and arrested before he can finish Gumbi It ended up looking like I was involved in this, but it was actually them. Voice over five A conservation researcher, and key witness questions the narrative. Alice Wild Anyone who has tried to shine any light on this story, has either been assassinated or intimidated, their reputations destroyed. Voice over six And questions raised on the role of a wildlife NGO and its high profile founder. Claire If it turned out to be true then how were they all acquitted? Jamie This is South Africa! How are they all acquitted? How are they always all acquitted? Alice Wild South Africans wanted a perpetrator, they loved her story. She published a photograph of a naked man, bleeding from being shot and the SA audience loved it FADE TO BLACK OVER PHOTOGRAPH. Voice over seven In 2014, former crime intelligence officer, Christopher Gumbi, was deployed in Jozini, to help combat organised crime along the border with Mozambique. Christopher Gumbi While we were working, crimes were being committed right under our noses. These crimes were organised by professionals. We were there working as Crime Intelligence, look at it like this my sister, Crime Intelligence versus Organised (Crime.) These are both heavyweights. Voice over eight It appeared to him that Mozambicans were being framed by members of organised crime. Gumbi They took people across the border. They would bring them into the reserve, foreigners from Mozambique. They were then found murdered inside the reserves and accused of rhino poaching. Voice over nine What Gumbi saw at the scenes didn't make sense. Gumbi Then you find that person lying dead. The rhino horn is missing. Who took the rhino horn? How? This kept happening. That is when my focus shifted. Claire So you have identified it was organised crime, was that a shock to you? Gumbi Yes that is how it was. I was confused. Our colleagues are doing this. Our white colleagues. Were they using their skin colour to pull this off? And I decided that something needs to be done, no one is above the law. Voice over ten But soon afterwards he was arrested using what’s known as an entrapment warrant. Issued by the National Prosecuting Authority, they’re used to detect, investigate or prevent an offence. Gumbi was arrested by this man- JP Van Zyl Roux and charged with the unlawful possession of rhino horns, fraud and robbery. In an instant, Gumbi’s life and reputation were destroyed. Clair What would you like to see happen? Gumbi I want the truth to be revealed. Voice over 11 A court and an internal disciplinary hearing later found Gumbi not guilty. But he waited years before the high court ruled he'd been an honest witness and awarded him damages. Link The judgement in favour of Mr Gumbi says that the SAPS member that issued the warrant of entrapment behaved dishonestly, unlawfully, maliciously pursuing a fruitless prosecution, but what is clear is that this was a pattern and the victims were usually poor and black Voice over 12 When Wiseman Mageba sat down with us he was nervous. He hasn't told his story before. Wiseman Mageba I am very afraid.. I never know when they will come for me.... They can come at any time to shoot me as happened to other Voice over thirteen In 2014, Mageba was arrested in 2014.. At the time he owned a construction business and crucially to our investigation, an electrician he used called Dumisani Gwala, was arrested on the same day. Up sound Mageba was arrested while fixing his car at the side of the road. Officially he was suspected of carrying rhino horn but in this police video of his arrest, there’s no sign of it. Mageba claims that, at one point the police put a bag in his car. Up sound After asking what they were doing, these heavily armed men arrived and took him into custody. Up sound of the arrest. Van Zyl Roux- the officer who’s arrested crime intelligence officer, Christopher Gumbi - was central to this arrest too. He says Mageba and the electrician, Dumisani Gwala, bought rhino horn from police agents. But our investigation revealed that this man, one of the agents, is a former crime intelligence officer, fired for extortion in 2021. Voice over 14 Mageba spent 838 days in a police cell. Mageba Two years, three months is a long time. On the 28th of July 2023, it's where we finalised the case, it's where the judgement came to us. Voice over 15 In 2023 he was found not guilty. All ten charges ruled to be inadmissible. Mageba I lost my everything. I lost my company, my family, my wife and kids, so that was a very bad time for me. Voice over 16 The court questioned what had happened to the 6 rhino horns used by the police, why there had been no paper trail, or attempt to infiltrate the alleged syndicate he was supposed to be a part of. Mageba Then I said oh thank God. Actually we are the victims. They need to get the victims to cover themselves Voice over 17 Dumisani Gwala was shot at 11 times during his arrest. Six bullets hit their mark Gwala The way things panned out, their intention was to kill me. Voice over 17 He was, according to the police, the rhino poaching kingpin. Claire As we sit here today, you didn’t want to talk to us, why not? Dumisani Gwala I have suffered a lot, with my family, a lot. Even now I am not sleeping at home. I sleep in the forest. What has happened is that we were paraded in the media, the whole world knows my face. Voice over 18 And the reason his face is so well known, is down to a wildlife activist called Jamie Joseph. A South African who is the founder of Saving the Wild, an NGO registered in New Zealand, she built a campaign around Gwala, raising over a million US Dollars Jamie Joseph He is responsible for 80% of the horns that go through KZN province. Dumisani Gwala Jamie Joseph, she's an animal. I don't have the power to do anything to her. When I see her I have to run, because I never know what she is going to do. Link Convict Dumisani Gwala as a rhino poaching kingpin is her mantra, and a movie about her campaign is being planned. Except there is a problem, Jamie Joseph’s ending is not working out quite as she had hoped. Gwala has been acquitted, and now has a damages claim against the state Alice Wild She would follow Dumisane Gwala into the lavatories, Dumisani Gwala would say leave me alone and the next day they would print a picture in the Newspaper to say Dumisani Gwala threatens the journalist Claire What was the purpose of your campaign on social media when it came to Dumisani Gwala? Jamie Joseph People needed to understand that he had all these magistrates on his payroll and police officers and we thought that if we put it in the public domain and gave it a big enough spotlight, we hoped that he wouldn’t get away with it. Claire So do you have evidence that Dumisani Gwala had magistrates on their payroll. Do we know that for a fact Jamie Joseph Of course. It was all over the news, the person who was paying the bribes to the magistrate and the prosecutors and taking money from people like Gwala and police officer Gumbi was the defence attorney’s nephew, Voice over 19 The evidence Joseph is referring to, came from a single whistleblower who claims to have handed money to magistrates on Gwala’s behalf. Jamie Joseph So the whistleblower came forward and he actually gave one exclusive interview to BBC and the sworn affidavit, after that he did a polygraph and the police investigated everything he said in his affidavit and it all turned out to be true. Voice over 20 Except the whistleblower is a criminal and was in jail at the time he claimed to be handing cash to the magistrates. He later retracted his statement in an affidavit. Alice Wild It's very reminiscent of an apartheid style disinformation campaign, so everything that is ever said you can turn around 180% round. Voice over 21 Joseph seems to have mastered the art of blending fact with fiction. Take for example the official police video of Gwala’s arrest, which I had not seen when I interviewed her. Jamie Joseph Have you seen the arrest video? Claire No I haven’t. Jamie Joseph He wasn’t viciously attacked. He was the one beating a police officer to death Claire To death? Jamie Joseph In the video you see the horns being thrown and beating this police officer almost to death. Voice over 22 In affidavits, the police said they were going to Gwala’s house to collect the money from undercover deals they’d done with him, and to hand over another horn for the next deal. But in the police video which we have slowed down, there is no evidence of money changing hands. What can be seen is the fired crime intelligence officer in a red shirt placing a bag into Gwala’s boot. Gwala removes the bag and pushes it back at the officer, who then opens the drivers side of the car and leans in. He is still holding the bag and Gwala appears confused. GWALA Right after that I saw a policeman come out of the back of their car and started shooting at me, that’s how I got arrested. That is how I lost everything. Up sound video Get down wena Voice over 23 The police grab Gwala and say get down dog, we are going to shoot you. A scuffle ensues and a horn appears on the ground. We don't know how it gets there, and we don't see- as Jamie Joseph told me, Gwala almost beating a cop to death. Carte Blanche has gone through the video frame by frame and it shows Gwala trying to get away, his wheels spinning in the sand as 3 weapons are pointed at him. He is unarmed and shot at eleven times. Up sound Shoot that guy man! Shoot that bastard. Shots fired. Voice over 24 Eight years after his arrest, the courts found the evidence against Gwala inadmissible. Crucially it found that at no stage had either of the accused sold rhino horns. Gwala was found not guilty on all counts except a charge of resisting arrest. Claire To be honest your campaign went in hard. Would you apologise to him if you were told that you were wrong? Jamie Joseph I wasn’t wrong! Voice over 25 Van Zyl Roux, the investigating officer, believes he wasn't wrong either. He says the evidence was not admitted because of a technicality. In a written answer to us, he added that Gumbi’s claims of his involvement in organised crime are libellous and denied. Mageba and Gwala still live in fear. There are unexplained deaths. In 2023, a businessman called Mackson Chirwa, who helped pay their legal costs was assassinated. His murder remains unsolved Up sound Mackson Chirwa Why are you taking the photos because you don't know me. No, I am not shouting. Voice over 26 Jamie Joseph says she was accosted by him outside Court, but this video suggests that he was asking her to stop filming him. He filed an intimidation charge against her. Jamie Joseph Gwala, he lives by the gun, he will die by the gun. He will end up the same way his business partner, the hitman ended up. I am more worried about the sanctity of the courts. Voice over 27 Joseph doesnt trust the judgements we have relied upon. She is determined to prove her claims of corrupt court officials and says the judgements are baseless. She is astounded that we’re questioning her narrative. Jamie Joseph But the way you were talking about Gwala it's like he got to somebody, and his hitman and business partner have very high connections in politics? Claire So are you saying Carte Blanche is being influenced? What are you saying? Jamie Joseph I don't know who Gwala can get to, ok? Claire So he got to Carte Blanche in your mind? Jamie Joseph It sounds to me like you are trying to create a story to make Gwala look good Voice over 28. The investigating officer, JP Van Zyl Roux was fired from the police in 2017. He says the reason for his dismissal was unrelated to this case and he was unfairly dismissed. He denied he received any bonuses from the police, and that the imputation of apartheid era police tactics are vexatious and scurrilous. Meanwhile the movie inspired by Jamie Joseph, continues. Claire Let's talk about your movie that is in the pipeline? Jamie Joseph Why are we talking about my movie? Claire Because I want to wrap it up, you said you wanted to know if we are going to talk about JJ But now it sounds like there is a witch-hunt and I dont know yet because we will see what the final thing looks like, we will see if all my stuff is edited you know… Claire Do you want to talk to us or not Jamie? Jamie Joseph Because we wouldn't have lost all those rhino’s if we had people like JP Roux working in KZN and Gwala was locked up in jail, but keep going! Claire Actually I think I am done. I think I am actually done! Ya Voice over 29 Gwala and Mageba are taking the Minister of Police, Minister of Justice and the NPA to court, claiming wrongful and unlawful arrest, entrapment, torture, and attempted murder. Our questions to SAPS remain unanswered. The NPA says that due to the pending civil suit they will not be commenting. KZN’s rhinos are still being killed. In 2023, 307 rhinos were lost in Hluhluwe iMfolozi Parks. There were 49 arrests made. THE END 18 minutes PROMO ONE Voice over Men accused of being KZN’s rhino poaching kingpins speak out for the first time after being acquitted Alice Wild 22 00 People didn’t bother to ever check, the same story was repeated over and over but who would believe a black man, uneducated against a white Afrikaans policeman whose father was a brigadier Up sound Jamie Joseph Dumisani Gwala is a rhino poaching kingpin you have never heard of. He is responsible for 80% of the horns that go through KZN province. Voice over And a self styled corruption buster who ran a campaign against them is unapologetic Claire To be honest your campaign went in hard so I am saying would you apologise to him if you were told that you were wrong? JAMIE JOSEPH I wasn’t wrong! PROMO TWO A man accused of being an accomplice to a rhino poaching kingpin, lost everything when he was wrongly arrested. A decade later he speaks out Mageba Then I stayed there almost the rest of my life, two years, three months Claire whispers Two years and three months? Mageba Since 2014, until on the 28th of July 2023, it's where we finalised the case and the judgement came to us. And a former warrant officer stumbles across crime scenes that point to his colleagues. Gumbi Then you find that person shot and the rhino horn is missing. They are lying dead, who took the rhino horn? How? This kept happening. Claire So you have identified it was organised crime, was that a shock to you? Gumbi Yes that is how it was. I was confused. Our colleagues are doing this. Our white colleagues. Were they using their skin colour to pull this off? And I decided that something needs to be done, no one is above the law. PROMO THREE Voice over They were called the rhino poaching kingpins. Wiseman Mageba I am very afraid.. I never know when they will come for me.... They can come at any time to shoot me as happened to other Voice over It took a decade in the courts, and they lost everything. For the first time the men at the heart of this story, speak to Carte Blanche Gwala Their intention was to kill me. Claire To be honest your campaign went in hard so I am saying would you apologise to him if you were told that you were wrong? JAMIE JOSEPH I wasn’t wrong!

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Rogue cops, an antipoaching unit, extrajudicial killings to claim bonuses and danger pay. The story of two building contractors and a good cop, whose lives were destroyed when they were set up as rhin
metadata.Unique Selling Point: The case studies will go on camera, we have unseen footage, and all the court documents vindicating the men who claimed innocence for over 9 years but were smeared by an NGO with ulterior motives.
metadata.Summary: Overview Around 2014, police officer Christopher Gumbi was seconded to take part in a rural safety operation in the Jozini cluster. He had already been involved in the process of gathering information about an operation involving the rendition of foreign nationals from Mozambique being lured into game parks in KZN and then killing them under the guise of those persons being suspected of being involved in rhino horn poaching. The purpose of the persons involved in the rendition and the murder of foreign nationals was to recover rewards paid to informers and recover danger allowances. But Gumbi was a problem to a group of police and private security who had a lot to hide and a lot to lose, because they were doing just that- cashing in on money from an NGO and danger pay from the police, by falsely accusing innocent victims of rhino poaching. Their victims -and the stories of Wiseman Mageba and Dumisani Gwala if exposed would pose a threat to the rogue police and their security buddies who claim to be hero’s saving the rhino, when all they were really doing was lining their own pockets. Our story weaves Gumbi’s story with that of Gwala and Mageba. All three have been vindicated by the courts and we have all the documents. Gumbi has already been paid damages, but he left the police. In July 2023 Gwala and Mageba were vindicated by the courts and now they have in Feb 2024 served summons against SAPS and the NPA for a large damages claim.
metadata.Further information: WISEMAN MAGEBA AND DUMISANI GWALA. Gwala was set up by Warrant officer JP Roux and an agent who later mysteriously died. The rhino horn from KZN Ezemvelo Parks that was used to set him up disappeared. When he was arrested he was shot eleven times in front of his pregnant wife and his seven year old daughter. Gwala should have died, but he didn’t. His wife later lost her child from the stress of everything. ( there is footage from the shooting that has never been seen – it comes from the police bodycam and we have access to this footage) His case was manipulated and moved from one court to another and when it became clear in 2016 that the court case would reveal the shocking truth that Gwala and Mageba were falsely arrested so that the rogue cops could cash in on the danger pay and the bonusses for arresting rhino poachers, they paid an NGO to smear the men. It was a full on apartheid style disinformation campaign, says Megan Carr, who at first thought Warrant officer JP ROUX and Jamie Joseph from the NGO Save the wild, were hero’s. But as she dug deeper using her own funds, she realized that in fact the real picture was quite different and Joseph was paid to muddy the water. Mostly the media lapped it up, and that is when Carr decided to go all in, and fund a good criminal lawyer to unearth the police footage and give her a true picture of events so she didn’t think she was going quite mad. Carte Blanche investigates this story that highlights the shadowy world of rogue cops, rhino horns, an apartheid style disinformation campaign and the difficulty that poor people falsely accused have when they come up against this shadow state.
